Toilet Paper

Claude writes a short source file. tp draws the picture, the process map or the Word document from it, the same way every time, in the D&A look, and says when a published file is older than its source.

No AI model insideRuns on your PC Nothing leaves NETZSCH29 layouts, 23,538 icons

Why the name

Napkin AI is a paid web app that turns text into nice pictures. The first version of this tool was a home-made copy of it. A home-made napkin is toilet paper.

How it works

Before and now

The 18 process maps of BIA-023, drawn by hand by an agent, and then by tp from the same content.

Before: drawn by hand

Arrows run through boxes, and "100% match" and "No match" sit on the lines.

Now: drawn by tp

Same 18 maps, counted the same way. The map that did not open was invalid XML written by an agent.

What it makes

Pictures29 layouts: steps, cycle, comparison, funnel, pyramid, timeline, numbers, 2x2 matrix, tree, hub, roadmap, mind map, converge, diverge, fan, path, ripple, chain, dialog, gauge, signpost, climb, layers, venn, iceberg, bridge, journey, cadence and puzzle.
Process mapsBPMN with lanes and decisions. The .bpmn opens in Camunda Modeler; no arrow crosses a box, no text sits on a line.
RACI matricesOne A per row, checked. Picture and markdown table from the same source.
Word documentsOfficial ones on the NETZSCH template; the rest with the 3 logos and a footer that says who made it, when and from what.
Checkstp check finds a published file older than its source; tp audit finds a Word file made around the tools.

Document templates

Pages of each, rendered by tp from the source below them. Copy a source and change the text.

Official

DA-POL, DA-STD, DA-SOP, DA-GDL, DA-GOV, DA-FRM, DA-REC, DA-TPL

The NETZSCH template as it is: its header with the logo, title and date, its footer with authors, version and page. It opens with a Summary of 50 words at most for the approver.

Source: OFFICIAL.md

# DA-GDL-99 Export of Confidential Reports

## Summary

A Confidential report is exported only after the Information Owner releases it. The owner checks the
responsibility term first. The workspace admin turns export on for that one report. Every year the owner
confirms the release still makes sense.

## Goal

Show the official template as tp fills it: the NETZSCH header and footer, numbered sections, a table and
figures drawn from their own source files.

## 1. Responsibilities

| Role | Rule |
|---|---|
| Information Owner | Decides who may export the data of a workspace |
| Workspace Admin | Applies the settings the owner decided |

The matrix shows who does what when a report owner asks for export.

![Figure 1. Responsibilities for an export release](../../diagrams/PBI-EXPORT.raci.yaml)

## 2. Process

The owner answers within 5 working days. Without an answer, the request stays closed.

![Figure 2. Workspace onboarding](../../diagrams/ONBOARD.bpmn.yaml)

# Report Usage Review

## Which reports people open, and which ones nobody opens

## Summary

12 of 40 reports had no viewer in 90 days. We propose to archive them after their owners confirm. The
other 28 stay, and the 5 most used get a quarterly review.

## 1. Purpose and scope

This review covers the reports of one workspace from July to September. It counts views per report and
names the owner of each one.

> A report with no viewer in 90 days is a candidate to archive, not a decision. The owner decides.

## 2. Findings

| Group | Reports | Views in 90 days |
|---|---|---|
| Most used | 5 | 2,140 |
| In use | 23 | 610 |
| No viewer | 12 | 0 |

![Figure 1. How a confidential report gets export](../../visuals/EXPORT-REQUEST.visual.yaml)

## 3. Next steps

The owners of the 12 reports confirm or keep each one until the end of November.

> **Attention:** an archived report leaves the app for its viewers. The owner keeps a copy.

# Sales Reporting Phase 2

## Summary

The project replaces 4 manual sales reports with one data model and one report. The sales team stops building
spreadsheets by hand each month. It starts in November and ends in March. The sponsor approves the scope now and
the result at the end.

## 1. Project Purpose and Objectives

**Purpose:** each month the sales team spends 3 days building 4 reports by hand, and the numbers differ between them.

**Objective:** by 31 March 2027, one report on one data model replaces the 4 reports, and the monthly close takes
half a day.

## 2. Scope and Key Deliverables

**In scope:** sales orders and invoices of the 2 plants, the 4 current reports, access by role.

**Out of scope:** forecasting, other business units.

- A data model with orders and invoices
- One report with the views of the 4 current reports
- Access groups by role
- A short guide for the sales team

## 3. Project Manager and Executive Sponsor

| Role | Name | Department/Title | Contact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project Manager | Ana Example | Data and Analytics | ana@example.com |
| Executive Sponsor | Sponsor Example | Head of Sales | sponsor@example.com |

## 4. Stakeholder Identification

| # | Stakeholder Name | Title/Role | Influence Level | Details/Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sponsor Example | Head of Sales | High | Approves scope and result |
| 2 | Sales controllers | Users | Medium | Validate the numbers |

Who does what is in the RACI matrix of the project, not in this charter.

## 5. High-Level Requirements

- The report shows the same totals as the invoice system
- Each person sees only the plants of their role

## 6. Key Milestones and Timeline

| # | Milestone | Target Date | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope approved | 15.11.2026 | Ana Example | Planned |
| 2 | Data model validated | 31.01.2027 | Ana Example | Planned |
| 3 | Report in use | 31.03.2027 | Ana Example | Planned |

## 7. Assumptions and Constraints

**Assumptions:** the invoice system keeps its current structure until March.

**Constraints:** the team has 1 developer for this project.

## 8. Risks

| # | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Totals differ from finance | Occasional | High | Compare with finance every 2 weeks | Ana Example |

## 9. Success Metrics

| # | Category | Metric | Target | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Effort | Days to close the month | 0.5 | Planned |
| 2 | Quality | Reports that disagree | 0 | Planned |

## 10. Definition of Ready (DoR)

- Business case approved
- Stakeholders identified
- High-level requirements documented

## 11. Definition of Done (DoD)

- All deliverables accepted
- Success metrics achieved
- Documentation completed
- Lessons learned recorded

## 12. Lessons Learned

Filled in at closure.

## 13. Approval Signatures

| Name | Role | Signature | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sponsor Example | Executive Sponsor | | |
| Ana Example | Project Manager | | |

# Example Area Governance

**Document number:** DA-GOV-99

**Version:** 0.1 (DRAFT)

**Classification:** Internal

## Summary

The area takes work through demands and tickets. Each demand has an owner in the business. A delivery is
finished when the owner accepts it and the documentation is filed. The approvers sign this document once a
year.

## Approval

| Version | Approval date | Approved by | Role | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | PENDING | Approver Example | CFO, Business Unit A | |
| 1.0 | PENDING | Approver Example | CFO, Business Unit B | |

## Versions

| Version | Release date | Modification | Responsible | Review due |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | DRAFT | First version | Data & Analytics | Annual from approval |

## 1 Purpose and scope

This document says how the area takes, runs and finishes work. It covers demands, tickets and the roles
that decide. It does not cover the group data governance framework.

## 2 How work enters

Work enters in 2 ways:

1. A demand, for new work with a business owner.
2. A ticket, for a fault or a small change.

![Figure 1. Workspace onboarding](../../diagrams/ONBOARD.bpmn.yaml)

## 3 When a delivery is finished

A delivery is finished when:

1. The business owner accepts it.
2. The documentation is filed.
3. The support team knows how to run it.

## 4 Change log

| Version | Date of the change | Responsible person(s) or team(s) | Description of the changes made | Approval details |

# Spare part quotes in one day

## For the CFOs of the business units. Decision asked: roll out to 2 more plants in Q1.

## Summary

Customers waited 6 days for a spare part quote. Since July, one plant answers in one day, and 3 in 10 quotes
became orders, up from 2 in 10. We ask to roll it out to 2 more plants in Q1. It needs no new hires.

## The problem

A customer who asks for a spare part waits 6 days for the price. In that time many buy from someone else.
The sales team copies the parts list of each machine by hand before it can quote.

## What changed

Since July, the parts list of every machine sold is ready when the customer asks. The sales team quotes the
same day.

| | Before | Since July |
|---|---|---|
| Days to quote | 6 | 1 |
| Quotes that became orders | 2 in 10 | 3 in 10 |

## What we ask

Agree to roll it out to 2 more plants in Q1. Each plant gives 2 days of one sales person to check the first
lists. No new hires, no new budget.

The parts lists come from the systems the plants already use.

# Status reports live in one place

## Summary

Every project status report goes into the project tool, every 15 days, also when all is green. The Word copy
is for people outside the tool. One place means the steering committee reads the same numbers the team sees.

## Context

Status reports reach the steering committee in 3 forms: the project tool, a slide and a spreadsheet. The 3 use
different health scales, so the same project can look green in one and yellow in another.

## Options considered

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| Keep the 3 forms | No change for anybody | The committee keeps reading 3 versions of one project |
| The project tool only | One record, the scale of the tool | People without access need a copy |
| The tool, plus a Word copy made from the same text | One record, and a copy for people outside the tool | The copy must never be edited by hand |

## Decision

The project tool is the record. A Word copy, when someone needs it, is made from the same text and is never
edited by hand.

## Consequences

The slide and the spreadsheet stop. Project managers fill in one form every 15 days. A health colour means the
same thing in every report.

# Move a report from test to production

## When to use it

When a report passed its test and the owner agreed to publish it. One report at a time.

## Before you start

- The owner wrote "approved" in the request.
- You can publish to the production workspace.
- The report has no personal test filter left on.

## Steps

1. Open the report in the test workspace and note its version.
2. Publish it to the production workspace with the same name.
3. Set the refresh to the time the owner asked for.
4. Give access to the groups in the request, never to single people.
5. Write the version and the date in the request and close it.

## Check

Open the report in production as a person of one of the groups. The numbers match the test version, and the
last refresh shows today.

## Change log

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 23.10.2026 | First version |

# Close the reports nobody opened in 90 days

## Summary

We ask to archive the 12 reports nobody opened in 90 days, after each owner confirms. If there is no answer
by 6 November, we only list them and archive nothing. Each report can come back in one day.

## What we ask

Agree that the 12 reports with no viewer since July are archived, each one after its owner confirms by e-mail.

## If you agree

The owners get one e-mail each next week. A report is archived 5 working days after its owner confirms. The
workspace keeps the 28 reports people use.

## If there is no answer

Nothing is archived. The list goes into the next status report, and we ask again in December.

## What stays open

3 of the 12 reports have no owner on record. They stay until someone claims them or the area head decides.

# Sales Reporting Phase 2, project closure

## Summary

The project delivered one data model and one report that replace 4 manual reports. The sponsor accepted all
deliverables on 20 October. It closed 2 weeks late and within budget. Go-live in plant B is the sales team's.

## Objectives and results

| Objective | Result |
|---|---|
| One report replaces the 4 manual reports | Done; the 4 reports stopped in September |
| The monthly close takes half a day | Done; it took 3 days before |

## Deliverables and acceptance

| Deliverable | Accepted by | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Data model for orders and invoices | Sponsor Example | 20.10.2026 |
| Sales report | Sponsor Example | 20.10.2026 |
| Short guide for the sales team | Sponsor Example | 20.10.2026 |

## Schedule and cost

Planned end 6 October, actual end 20 October: plant B data arrived 2 weeks late. Cost within the approved
hours.

## Benefits

The sales team saves 2.5 days a month on the close. The plant figures now match, so the monthly review starts
from one number.

## Lessons learned

- Repeat: test with the users of one plant before the second plant starts.
- Avoid: start without a date for the data of every plant.

## Open items

| Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Forecasting view, moved to a new request | Sponsor Example | Q1 |

## Handover

The team closes in Delivered. Go-live in plant B and the daily operation are the sales team's, with Ana
Example as solution owner.

# Sales Reporting Phase 3, handover to the new project manager

## Summary

Bruno takes over Sales Reporting Phase 3 from Ana on 3 November. The project is on schedule, with one risk
open on plant C data. Ana stays 2 weeks in overlap. The sponsor confirms the handover on 17 November.

## Current status

Planning is done and the baseline is approved. The first sprint starts on 3 November. Schedule and cost are
green; resources are yellow while one developer is shared.

## Documents

| Document | Where |
|---|---|
| Charter | Project folder, 01 Initiation |
| Status reports | The project tool |
| Risk register | The project tool |
| Decision log | Project folder, 02 Planning |

## Knowledge sessions

1. Project context and stakeholders, 28 October, recorded.
2. Data model and open design points, 30 October, recorded.

## Stakeholders and communication

The sponsor announces the change to the team on 31 October. Bruno meets each plant lead in his first week.

## Overlap

Ana stays 2 weeks: in week 1 Bruno leads with Ana present, in week 2 Bruno leads alone and Ana answers
questions.

## Open risks and decisions

Plant C invoice data may arrive late. The forecasting view waits for the sponsor's decision.

## Validation

The sponsor confirms on 17 November that Bruno has taken over. Ana's responsibility ends that day.

process map

BPMN with lanes; a node can take a tone.

Source: ONBOARD.bpmn.yaml
ai: none                        # drawn by hand from a written source; see docs/ai-label-rule.md
id: ONB01
name: Workspace onboarding with review loop
lanes:
  - {id: owner, name: Information Owner}
  - {id: admin, name: Workspace Admin}
  - {id: platform, name: D&A Platform}
nodes:
  - {id: start, type: start, lane: owner, name: New workspace needed}
  - {id: req, type: user, lane: owner, name: Fill in the workspace request}
  - {id: check, type: task, lane: platform, name: Check naming and classification,
     note: "Naming follows DA-STD-04. Classification decides who may export."}
  - {id: ok, type: xor, lane: platform, name: "Request complete?"}
  - {id: create, type: service, lane: admin, name: Create workspace and AD groups}
  - {id: split, type: and, lane: admin}
  - {id: roles, type: task, lane: admin, name: Assign workspace roles}
  - {id: app, type: task, lane: admin, name: Publish the app audience}
  - {id: join, type: and, lane: admin}
  - {id: done, type: end, lane: owner, name: Workspace live}
flows:
  - start -> req -> check -> ok
  - ok -> create : yes
  - ok -> req : no, back to owner
  - create -> split
  - split -> roles -> join
  - split -> app -> join
  - join -> done

Icons

Lucide 1.17.0 (ISC licence, 1713 icons); Phosphor 2.1.1 (names start with ph:, MIT licence, 4536 icons); Tabler 3.47.0 (names start with tb:, MIT licence, 6202 icons); Remix 4.9.1 (names start with rx:, Apache-2.0 licence, 3229 icons); Material 0.48.0 (names start with ms:, Apache-2.0 licence, 7858 icons). Use the name as icon: in a .visual.yaml.

Colours

The D&A palette the pictures use.

Accent #007167Brand colour, success state, first item of the ramp
Light blue #3D90B0End of the ramp, in-progress state
Orange #E27B00Attention state; bar or icon only, never small text
Grey #7D868FNeutral state
Ink #4C4D57Every text
Slate #263240Text and icons on orange; the NETZSCH logo
Page #F2F2F2Page ground
Toilet Paper 2.18.2
